content.comment_body: Hello, I've searched the forum and tried all suggested solutions, but I can't upload my programs to the [product_name]. No matter what program I attempt, I always get a log message: "Download PC --> [product_name] failed" with no further details. Other functions like IP settings, reading the clock, setting up and connecting to the web server, and reading analog inputs online all work fine. I'm using Mac OS Ventura 13.4 but also tested on Windows 10 and 11, with the same issue across each. Connection via ethernet is established successfully, yet every attempt to upload fails. Am I missing something? [product_name] firmware [version_no] ([article_no]) [product_name] software [version_no] (full version)
I've attached a PDF screenshot from the online help. It lists which operating systems the [product_name] software was tested with.
For Windows 10: Did you install the [product_name] software as an administrator? Are your [product_name] device and PC/Laptop in the same subnet?

Yes, they're on the same subnet with the correct gateway. It's strange because I can connect, go online in network mode, display all real-time I/O values, and see them change. Just the program upload doesn't succeed. Everything else works fine except uploading the program. I'll try my old Windows 8 PC to see if it works there.
Is your hardware configuration correct? In your setup, is the [product_name] version set to [version_no] in the hardware selection?
Could you please upload your program as a ZIP file?

I tested with sample programs, even made a simple one that displays analog input as text. After switching to my old PC, everything worked fine. I apologize for not trying it sooner, as I assumed it would work because other features did. Windows 8 solved the problem (unlike enterprise Windows 10). Thank you for your help, and sorry for the oversight. It is unfortunate the software doesn't support newer operating systems well.
The software works correctly with current Windows OS; make sure to review your network settings. Is your PC's network type set to local? Did you allow the firewall changes when prompted?

I see things differently. It's disappointing that Microsoft's approach neglects support for older software. Developers nearly always must update to the newest SDK to ensure compatibility with a constantly evolving operating system. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing consistent failures uploading programs from PC to [product_name], even though network diagnostics and web server connectivity work seamlessly. The main issue appears on modern operating systems (Windows 10, Windows 11, MacOS Ventura), but resolves when using Windows 8. Users express frustration over compatibility between [product_name] software and recent OS versions, with seamless device communication not translating into successful program uploads.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable upload functionality to [product_name] devices across all supported and modern operating systems. They believe program transfer should work as smoothly as device communications once network connectivity is confirmed.
